coverageNote.note: Audited all 6 identifiable facilities (1 additional were unresolvable from public sources).

sites.name: Bob Evans Farms - Xenia OH Plant
sites.type: Manufacturing plant (fresh pork sausage rolls & links)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied geocode (39.680221, -83.911228, GEOMETRIC_CENTER) landed directly
on the plant complex. Satellite probes at z16-z20 show a multi-section
industrial / food-processing building with rooftop process equipment, an
employee parking lot to the north, and a paved truck yard to the east.
Street View (captured 2022-06) along Birch Rd shows the building branded
"Bob Evans" in the company's signature red script on both the west office wing
(with red awning and US flag) and the main plant wall — positive ID. Web
research corroborates: 640 Birch Rd is the historic Xenia sausage plant, in
operation since 1953, ~30,000 sq ft core, >100 employees, ~30M lb/yr fresh
product; subject of a $6.15M expansion announced April 2014. This is the
plant, not a restaurant. Note: a Yelp listing tags this address as "CLOSED" —

fieldNotes.truckGate: East-side truck yard opens directly onto Birch Rd with no barrier arm, gate, or checkpoint. Street View (2022-06) confirms a wide-open paved apron meeting the public road. The west office/parking driveway is also an open curb cut. No truck gate.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No booth structure of any kind at either driveway. Confirmed in Street View from multiple headings.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Plant fronts directly on Birch Rd with minimal setback; the truck approach from road to dock is short, holding only 1-2 trucks.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimated 6 visible loading/overhead doors on the east and south building faces from satellite z20 and Street View; older small-footprint plant (~30,000 sq ft core). Low confidence on exact count due to building face angles.
fieldNotes.dropArea: No marked trailer-parking stalls; the east apron is open paved space, not a drop lot.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town Xenia surrounded by farm fields, ball fields, and scattered rural residential; classified Rural.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: East paved apron could informally hold ~8 trailers but has no marked stalls; low confidence.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Single connected/multi-section plant complex counted as ~4 distinct attached structures plus accessory equipment buildings.

sites.name: Bob Evans Farms - Lima OH Plant
sites.type: Manufacturing plant (refrigerated sides - mashed potatoes & macaroni & cheese; former Kettle Creations facility)

steps.step: Arrive at gate (no guard, kiosk or call box)

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied geocode (40.696965, -84.095537, ROOFTOP) landed on the large plant
building. Satellite at z16-z20 shows a single very large connected
food-processing building with extensive trailer parking. Street View along
Commerce Pkwy (captured 2024-10) shows the building branded "Bob Evans" in red
script on the west elevation — positive ID. Note: the smaller white building
immediately to the west is a separate company, "Logoplaste" (plastics
packaging), clearly labeled in Street View — it was excluded from the audit.
Web research confirms 651 Commerce Pkwy is the former Kettle Creations plant,
acquired by Bob Evans in August 2012 for $50M; ~150,000 sq ft after expansions,
~300 employees, 5 production lines, ~130M lb/yr of mashed potatoes and mac &
cheese.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Single truck driveway off Commerce Pkwy crosses a chain-link perimeter fence; a gate opening is visible in the fence line at satellite z21 (~40.6953, -84.0952). The whole trailer yard is fenced. Truck gate confirmed.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No booth structure visible beside the gate in satellite z20/z21 or in Street View (2024-10) from the road. Street View coverage does not extend up the private drive; absence of a booth at the fence crossing is the basis for the call. Flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Gate present but no guard shack -> remote/unmanned check-in implied (sliding gate / call-box / app).
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Long paved drive and a wide internal apron between the gate and the dock bank give ample inside-the-fence staging room.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Gate-to-dock approach is a long deep drive that can hold 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Large dock bank on the south building face with ~12-15 trailers backed in plus additional doors; estimated ~28 doors total. 25-50 band; exact count uncertain from overhead angles.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Multiple dedicated trailer-storage lots on the NE and SE of the property, full of parked trailers without tractors; well over 50 trailer stalls visible.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage lots clearly present on the NE and SE corners.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town industrial park on the south edge of Lima near I-75, bordered by farm fields; classified Rural.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: ~55 trailers visible in the imagery; lots could hold ~70. Estimate.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: One large ~150,000 sq ft connected plant building (the adjacent Logoplaste building to the west is a separate company, excluded).

sites.name: Bob Evans Farms - Hillsdale MI Plant
sites.type: Manufacturing plant (fresh pork sausage rolls & patties; USDA FSIS inspected)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied geocode (41.921573, -84.615533, GEOMETRIC_CENTER) landed on the
plant complex. Satellite at z16-z20 shows a multi-building food-processing
campus set well back from public roads, surrounded by residential streets,
farm fields, and woodland on the edge of Hillsdale. Street View (captured
2024-09) from the SW access road shows a "Bob Evans Farms" entrance sign and
the plant building branded with Bob Evans red script — positive ID. Note: the
address "200 N Wolcott St" is the postal address, but Wolcott St itself is
residential and the plant is set back behind houses; the actual truck/vehicle
access is a long private drive that connects to a side street SW of the site.
Web research confirms this is the company's third plant, producing fresh pork
sausage since 1964, 50+ SKUs, 25M+ lb/yr; BEF Foods operates it as a sow

fieldNotes.truckGate: Plant set well back from public roads on a long private access drive that connects to a residential side street SW of the site. The entrance has a Bob Evans Farms sign and decorative split-rail fence along the road, but the driveway is an open curb cut with no barrier arm, gate, or pinch-point. Confirmed in Street View (2024-09).
fieldNotes.guardShack: No booth structure at the entrance drive or anywhere on the access path; confirmed in Street View and satellite.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: No gate, so no remote check-in implied.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long private access drive from the public road to the plant; ample queue depth (3+ trucks).
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large internal paved courtyard and yard between the access drive and the dock buildings provides ample staging room.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Docks distributed across multiple building faces (central dock buildings + east building); ~16 doors estimated. Older multi-building campus; exact count uncertain from overhead angles.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Trailer drop yard on the NE of the property with ~10-14 trailers parked without tractors.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage area on the NE corner, separate from the dock aprons.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of 5 distinct buildings: main west plant, connected processing building, central dock buildings, and a separate east building.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Small-town Hillsdale, MI; the plant is on the edge of town surrounded by residential streets, farm fields, and woodland. Classified Rural.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: NE drop yard plus internal yard could hold ~25 trailers; estimate.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Counted ~5 distinct structures on the campus.

sites.name: Bob Evans Farms - Sulphur Springs TX Plant
sites.type: Manufacturing plant (refrigerated sides, including Bob Evans Macaroni & Cheese)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied geocode (33.129289, -95.580222, ROOFTOP) landed on the plant
building. Satellite at z16-z20 shows a large connected industrial building
beside Interstate 30, with a distinctive red-roofed section, open paved truck
yard, and employee parking. Street View along Industrial Dr E (captured
2025-06) shows the building branded "Bob Evans" in red script — positive ID.
Web research confirms 1109 Industrial Dr E is the Bob Evans Sulphur Springs
ready-to-eat plant, acquired in 2003, ~70 employees, producing refrigerated
sides (mac & cheese, mashed potatoes).

fieldNotes.truckGate: Two open driveways off Industrial Dr E (front employee/visitor drive and a west truck drive). Both are open curb cuts with no barrier arm, gate, or pinch-point. Confirmed in Street View (2025-06) — no perimeter fence around the property.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No booth at either driveway. A covered shelter near the parking lot is a carport/break shelter, not a guard booth.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: No gate, so no remote check-in implied.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Large open paved yard between Industrial Dr E and the south dock face gives deep approach room (3+ trucks).
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Wide open paved truck yard on the south/west of the building provides ample internal staging.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: South-facing dock bank with ~5-6 angled dock bays with trailers backed in, plus additional doors along the building face; ~12 doors estimated. 10-25 band; exact count uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: A few trailers parked near the dock apron without tractors; no dedicated striped drop lot. 0-10 band.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town industrial area along I-30 near Sulphur Springs, TX, bordered by farm fields and scattered industrial buildings; classified Rural.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Open paved yard could hold ~15 trailers informally; estimate.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: One large connected plant building plus an attached/adjacent processing wing — counted as ~2 structures.

sites.name: Bob Evans Farms - Rigby ID Plant
sites.type: Manufacturing plant (refrigerated and frozen potato products; Potato Products of Idaho facility absorbed under Post Holdings)
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied geocode (43.684086, -111.900523, ROOFTOP) landed on the plant
complex. Satellite at z16-z20 shows a large multi-building potato-processing
plant along N Yellowstone Hwy, surrounded by farm fields with a highway
interchange nearby. Web research confirms 398 N Yellowstone Hwy is the Potato
Products of Idaho (PPI) plant — a frozen/dehydrated potato-products
manufacturer established 1998, acquired by Post Holdings (parent of the Bob
Evans Refrigerated Retail business). The roster note matches: Post folded PPI
into the Refrigerated Retail network. Street View from the frontage road
showed an adjacent "BV's PRODUCE" sign (Rigby Produce, a neighboring business)
— the PPI plant itself is the large building cluster, positively located.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Plant accessed via open gravel/paved yards off N Yellowstone Hwy frontage; multiple open driveways with no barrier arm, gate, or checkpoint pinch-point. No perimeter fence around the property. Confirmed in satellite z19-z20.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No booth structure at any driveway or on the access yards.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: No gate, so no remote check-in implied.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Large open gravel/paved truck yards give deep approach room (3+ trucks).
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Extensive open paved/gravel yard between the highway and the plant buildings provides ample internal staging.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Dock activity concentrated at the building's west end where trucks load; few discrete dock doors visible (~10). Potato processors often load via fewer high-throughput doors and bulk infeed; exact count uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: A small number of trailers in the west-end yard without tractors; no large striped drop lot. 0-10 band.
fieldNotes.dropYard: An informal trailer-staging area exists at the building's west end, treated as a small drop yard.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of ~4 distinct structures: main processing plant, attached/adjacent buildings, and separate potato-storage cellar buildings to the south.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail line runs parallel to N Yellowstone Hwy along the north of the property, but it does NOT spur into the plant -- a drainage canal separates the property from the rail corridor. railServed false.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural Rigby, ID; the plant is surrounded by farm fields with a highway interchange nearby. Classified Rural.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: Few trailers visible in 2021/2026 imagery (~3); count uncertain.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Open yards could hold ~20 trailers informally; estimate.

sites.name: Bob Evans Farms - Springfield OH Transportation Hub
sites.type: Distribution / transportation hub (private fleet terminal - Bob Evans Transportation Company LLC, USDOT 911163; ~100 tractor-trailers)

steps.step: Arrive at gate (no guard, kiosk or call box)

sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied geocode (39.837963, -83.857367, ROOFTOP) landed on a fleet
terminal — a central dispatch/maintenance building flanked by extensive rows
of parked trailers. Web research confirms 6088 Green-Field Dr is the Bob Evans
Transportation Company LLC terminal (USDOT 911163): ~150 employees including
~100 drivers, ~126 tractors, 100+ tractor-trailers, ~20,000 deliveries/yr,
~10M miles/yr. The satellite layout — a terminal building with trailer-storage
rows on both sides — is exactly consistent with a private fleet hub. Positive
ID.

fieldNotes.imagery: Only available satellite coverage of this site is heavy snow-cover imagery, which obscures fine ground detail (gate hardware, booths, lane markings). No Street View coverage reaches the property. Overall confidence set to medium.
fieldNotes.truckGate: This is a private fleet terminal (Bob Evans Transportation Company, USDOT 911163; ~126 tractors, 100+ tractor-trailers, 20,000 deliveries/yr). The terminal is reached via an internal campus road off Green-Field Dr. A controlled truck entrance is the strong norm for a private fleet hub of this scale, but the gate hardware cannot be positively confirmed in the snow imagery -- flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth could be resolved in the snow imagery. Set false (no booth seen) but flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Given a probable gate and no visible booth, remote check-in is the best inference; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive trailer-parking rows on both sides of the central terminal building; well over 50 trailers -- this is the dominant feature of the site.
fieldNotes.dropYard: The whole site functions as a fleet trailer yard / terminal.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long internal campus road from Green-Field Dr to the terminal; ample queue depth.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: This is a fleet terminal, not a DC dock building; only a few service/maintenance bays on the central dispatch/shop building (~4). Not a loading-dock operation.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~120 trailers estimated in the parking rows from z17-z19 snow imagery; count approximate.
fieldNotes.trailerParkingCapacity: Marked rows could hold ~160 trailers; estimate.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural -- the terminal sits on the edge of Springfield surrounded by farm fields.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Central dispatch/maintenance building plus an accessory structure; ~2 (the large SW building is part of the wider distribution-center campus and treated as separate from the fleet terminal proper).
